observations: Photo 0 shows two power banks lying on a concrete floor.
One power bank is wrapped heavily in masking/cellotape around its middle, obscuring any label or ports.
The other power bank has a dark plastic casing with visible scuff marks, a faint logo/button area that is not legible, and a small flashlight-style oval opening.
Two charging cables (blue and green paracord-style) are coiled near the units, not clearly attached to either unit.
No screen, LED indicator, or brand/model text is legible on either unit.
Background is a bare floor, consistent with an informal/scrap sale setting.

claims.evidence: photo 0 shows visibly worn, taped-up casings consistent with non-retail, salvage-grade units

risks.risk: Battery cells may be dead, swollen, or unsafe (fire/leak risk) since internals are hidden under tape
risks.proof: A photo of the battery cell removed from the casing, or a video of it holding charge/powering a device

risks.risk: Charging ports or output ports may be damaged or missing, cables shown may not even belong to these units
risks.proof: A close-up photo of each unit's input/output ports and a clip showing a cable actually plugged in and charging a phone

risks.risk: Unknown mAh capacity and age, no model number visible to estimate original spec
risks.proof: A clear photo of any printed label/model sticker if one exists under the tape
risks.if_unproven: priced at lowest generic scrap-capacity assumption

proof_requests: Remove the tape and photograph the unit's label/ports/cells clearly
A video showing the power bank attempting to charge a phone, with any LED/indicator response
A photo of the battery cells themselves (swelling, leakage check)
response.reason: The items are identifiable as scrap power banks but no comparable listings exist to anchor even a worst-case price, and their internal condition cannot be judged from the photo.
